subject: general
question: The Golden Quadrilateral is associated with _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**roads**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral is a highway network connecting India's four major metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata.
 
• It is one of the largest highway projects in India and the fifth-longest in the world, with a total length of about 5,846 kilometers.
 
• The project was launched in 2001 under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) and was completed in 2012.
 
• This highway network facilitates efficient transportation and economic integration across the country, reducing travel time and vehicle operating costs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Highways Development Project (NHDP)**

 
 
• The NHDP is a project to upgrade, rehabilitate, and widen major highways in India to international standards.
 
• It is managed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and funded by the government of India, international organizations, and private sector investments.
 
• The NHDP includes several phases, with the Golden Quadrilateral being part of Phase I.
 
• The primary objective is to improve the efficiency of freight and passenger movement across the country, thus boosting the economy.
 
 
 
• **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**
 
 
• NHAI is an autonomous agency of the Government of India, responsible for the management of a network of over 50,000 km of National Highways.
 
• Established in 1988, it operates under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
 
• The agency's primary role is to develop, maintain, and manage the National Highways infrastructure in the country.
 
• NHAI is also involved in the implementation of various road infrastructure projects, including the NHDP.
 
 
 
• **Economic Benefits of Improved Road Infrastructure**
 
 
• Reduced travel time and fuel consumption for vehicles, leading to cost savings for businesses and consumers.
 
• Enhanced connectivity between cities and rural areas, promoting regional development and access to markets.
 
• Increased safety and reduction in road accidents due to better road conditions and infrastructure.
 
• Stimulation of economic activities along the highways, including the growth of logistics, tourism, and retail sectors.
